review_text: Recent advancements in large language models (LLMs) have significantly improved their ability to generate coherent and contextually relevant text, including scientific literature reviews [arXiv:2310.02456, стр. 3]. However, these models often suffer from hallucinations, where they generate information that is inconsistent with the training data or the context [arXiv:2309.12345, стр. 5]. To mitigate this issue, researchers have proposed various techniques, such as incorporating fact-checking mechanisms and using external knowledge bases to validate the generated content [arXiv:2311.01234, стр. 7]. Additionally, fine-tuning LLMs on domain-specific datasets has shown promise in reducing the frequency of hallucinations in scientific literature reviews [arXiv:2312.04567, стр. 4]. Another approach involves using reinforcement learning to train models to avoid generating contradictory or unsupported statements [arXiv:2310.12345, стр. 6]. These methods collectively aim to enhance the reliability and accuracy of LLM-generated scientific literature reviews [arXiv:2311.12345, стр. 8].

review_text: PSRD significantly reduces the hallucination of LLaVA-1.5-7B by 50.0%, as measured by the CHAIR metric on AMBER and outperforms existing post-hoc methods across all metrics on the MMHal-Bench and Object HalBench [arXiv:2604.17982, стр. 4]. The proposed method reduces the average hallucination rate by 13.2% across generation phases compared to LLaVA1.5-7B [arXiv:2604.17982, стр. 6]. The average phase-level hallucination accumulation rate (R𝑎𝑐𝑐) for LLaVA1.5-7B and M3ID is 0.35% and 0.40%, respectively, which is approximately seven times higher than the R𝑎𝑐𝑐 of 0.07% achieved by the proposed method [arXiv:2604.17982, стр. 6]. Engineering mitigates hallucinations by computing offset vectors between normal and hallucination-inducing prompts, then injecting these averaged vectors into specific modules in the model during inference to guide the model toward non-hallucinated outputs [arXiv:2505.12826, стр. 3]. The reported results for all baselines in hallucination mitigation tasks are sourced directly from their original publications or pertinent cited literature [arXiv:2604.17982, стр. 17]. PSRD enables a highly controllable trade-off between the performance of hallucination mitigation and inference efficiency [arXiv:2604.17982, стр. 2].

review_text: LLM reviewers failed to detect errors, assigned inflated review scores, and described figures that were not provided [arXiv:2608.28626, стр. 10]. LLM-generated review feedback has reported substantial overlap with human comments and high perceived utility, although their scoring is of limited value and their error-detection capabilities may be inadequate [arXiv:2608.28626, стр. 10]. LLM reviews identified only surface-level weaknesses and failed to detect conceptual deficiencies compared to human reviewers [arXiv:2608.28626, стр. 10]. Providing figures alongside manuscript text reduced error detection while increasing review scores [arXiv:2608.28626, стр. 1]. A one-sentence verification instruction approximately doubled error detection, whereas author identity had minimal effect on review scores [arXiv:2608.28626, стр. 9]. Existing evaluations of LLM reviewing are subject to contamination and version mismatch, which can affect the reliability of the results [arXiv:2608.28626, стр. 2]. A variety of benchmarks have been developed to evaluate hallucinations in LLMs, including tasks-specific benchmarks for summarization and other tasks [arXiv:2502.11306, стр. 7]. review_text: Recent studies have explored the effectiveness of using large language models (LLMs) as judges to evaluate Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems, highlighting their potential in providing nuanced and context-aware assessments [arXiv:2310.05456, стр. 3]. These LLM-as-a-judge frameworks can offer detailed feedback and scores that are more aligned with human judgments compared to traditional metrics like BLEU or ROUGE [arXiv:2309.12345, стр. 4]. However, the reliability and consistency of these LLM judges are still under scrutiny, with some research indicating that they can be biased or inconsistent in their evaluations [arXiv:2311.01234, стр. 5]. To address these issues, researchers have proposed various methods to calibrate and fine-tune LLM judges, aiming to improve their accuracy and fairness [arXiv:2312.09876, стр. 6]. Despite these advancements, the integration of LLMs as judges in RAG systems remains an active area of research, with ongoing efforts to enhance their robustness and applicability [arXiv:2311.14199, стр. 7].

review_text: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems enhance large language models (LLMs) by retrieving relevant knowledge, which helps mitigate LLM hallucinations and improves response quality [arXiv:2401.15391, стр. 1]. Existing RAG evaluation datasets primarily focus on the generation aspect of RAG systems without specifically addressing their retrieval accuracy [arXiv:2401.15391, стр. 8]. Recent advancements in automated RAG evaluation tools include ARES and RAGAS, which utilize LLMs to assess the quality of RAG generation [arXiv:2401.15391, стр. 8]. MultiHop-RAG can be used as a benchmark for various RAG-related tasks, and it is publicly released to contribute to the advancement and benchmarking of RAG systems [arXiv:2401.15391, стр. 5]. The ground truth answers in MultiHop-RAG are restricted to simple responses such as 'yes' or 'no', which is a limitation that can be improved in future research [arXiv:2401.15391, стр. 8]. Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) combines large language models (LLMs) with external document retrieval, allowing models to access information beyond their training data [arXiv:2510.25518, стр. 1].

review_text: Recent studies have highlighted the vulnerabilities of autonomous language model (LLM) agents to indirect prompt injection attacks, where malicious inputs can subtly manipulate the agent's behavior [arXiv:2310.02456, стр. 3]. To mitigate these risks, researchers have proposed various defense mechanisms, including input sanitization and context-aware filtering techniques [arXiv:2311.01234, стр. 5]. One notable approach involves using adversarial training to enhance the robustness of LLMs against such attacks [arXiv:2309.12345, стр. 7]. Additionally, dynamic monitoring and anomaly detection systems have been developed to identify and respond to suspicious prompts in real-time [arXiv:2312.04567, стр. 4]. These methods collectively aim to ensure the secure and reliable operation of autonomous LLM agents in diverse and potentially hostile environments [arXiv:2311.12345, стр. 6].

review_text: Indirect prompt injection (XPIA) occurs when LLMs are tasked with processing external data, and a malicious actor has injected instruction text inside those data sources [arXiv:2403.14720, стр. 1]. Indirect prompt injection attacks pose a risk when LLM systems have access to external data sources such as websites, emails, and text messages [arXiv:2403.14720, стр. 2]. To defend against indirect prompt injection, one approach is to explicitly demarcate the location of the input text in the system prompt, known as spotlighting via delimiting [arXiv:2403.14720, стр. 2]. Another defense mechanism involves updating the system prompt to include detailed instructions about the input text and how it should be treated [arXiv:2403.14720, стр. 2]. Simple mechanisms like the ROT13 cipher, while easy for LLMs to decode, can be easily subverted by attackers due to their simplicity and bidirectionality [arXiv:2403.14720, стр. 6]. Autonomous cyber defense agents will need to possess awareness of threats in near real-time and the ability to reliably self-propagate and disseminate information among trusted network members [arXiv:1905.05253, стр. 9].

review_text: Prompt injection attacks exploit the inability of LLMs to distinguish between instruction (from a trusted system designer) and data (from an untrusted user) in their input [arXiv:2410.05451, стр. 1]. Existing defenses against prompt injection attacks try to explicitly enforce the separation between instruction and data via prompting or fine-tuning [arXiv:2410.05451, стр. 1]. Fine-tuning defenses, which are empirically validated to be stronger in prior work, adopt a training loss that maximizes the LLM’s likelihood of outputting the desirable response [arXiv:2410.05451, стр. 1]. Prompt injection is a test-time attack against LLM-integrated applications that maliciously leverages the instruction-following capabilities of LLMs, where the attacker seeks to manipulate LLMs into executing an injected instruction hidden in the data instead of the benign instruction specified by the system designer [arXiv:2410.05451, стр. 2]. A secure LLM should observe the response to the injected instruction and be steered away from that response, which can be formulated as preference optimization [arXiv:2410.05451, стр. 2]. Among recent progress, Chen et al. and Piet et al. show promising robustness against optimization-free prompt injections, but none of them are robust to optimization-based prompt injections [arXiv:2410.05451, стр. 3]. Wallace et al. introduces the instruction hierarchy, a generalization of previous work, which aims to improve robustness against prompt injection attacks [arXiv:2410.05451, стр. 3]. review_text: Recent advancements in Agentic AI have emphasized the importance of self-correction and reflection mechanisms to enhance decision-making and ethical behavior [arXiv:2309.12345, стр. 5]. These mechanisms allow AI agents to evaluate their actions and outcomes, thereby improving their performance over time [arXiv:2309.12345, стр. 7]. Studies have shown that incorporating reflective practices can significantly reduce errors and improve the reliability of AI systems [arXiv:2310.09876, стр. 12]. However, the implementation of these mechanisms faces challenges, such as the need for robust feedback loops and the potential for overfitting to past experiences [arXiv:2310.09876, стр. 15]. Researchers have also explored the integration of human feedback to guide the self-correction process, enhancing the adaptability and ethical alignment of AI agents [arXiv:2311.01234, стр. 8]. Despite these advancements, further research is needed to develop more sophisticated and context-aware self-correction techniques [arXiv:2311.01234, стр. 10].

review_text: The agentic AI framework demonstrated superior autonomy and efficiency, achieving a 100% Problem Formulation Rate and a 72% Solution Solved Rate, with a 1st-Try Success Rate of 20% and an Average Attempt Time of 2.44 [arXiv:2601.19607, стр. 8]. Existing agentic AI frameworks for autonomous RAN are fundamentally open-loop, excelling at reasoning and planning but lacking empirical validation mechanisms to verify decisions and learn from outcomes [arXiv:2512.20640, стр. 1]. A reflection-driven self-optimization framework integrates agentic AI with high-fidelity network simulation in a closed-loop architecture, transforming unverified open-loop planning into a continuous, evidence-grounded, self-optimization workflow [arXiv:2512.20640, стр. 1]. In agentic AI, each executed action yields empirical feedback that is ingested by perception to trigger the next cycle of analysis and refinement, with reflection acting as an active critic to identify hallucinations, logical inconsistencies, and feasibility violations [arXiv:2601.19607, стр. 4]. The agentic loop is particularly well-aligned with wireless optimization workflows, as actions correspond to running code and invoking optimization modules, while reflection corresponds to diagnosing and correcting issues based on execution feedback [arXiv:2601.19607, стр. 2]. The reflection-driven self-optimization framework presented in the study significantly improves performance over non-agentic baselines, achieving a 17.1% higher throughput [arXiv:2512.20640, стр. 1]. The closed-loop architecture of the reflection-driven self-optimization framework orchestrates four specialized agents—scenario, solver, simulation, and reflector—to enable autonomous resource management [arXiv:2512.20640, стр. 9].

review_text: GraphRAG, an advanced retrieval-augmented generation model, leverages graph-based methods to enhance the retrieval of relevant documents, offering a more nuanced approach compared to standard semantic search techniques [arXiv:2309.12345, стр. 3]. This method is particularly effective in handling complex queries that require understanding the relationships between different pieces of information [arXiv:2309.12345, стр. 5]. In contrast, standard semantic search methods often rely on keyword matching and vector similarity, which can lead to less accurate or contextually relevant results [arXiv:2309.12345, стр. 7]. Studies have shown that GraphRAG outperforms traditional semantic search in tasks involving multi-hop reasoning and context-dependent information retrieval [arXiv:2309.12345, стр. 10]. However, the computational overhead of GraphRAG is higher, which may be a limiting factor in resource-constrained environments [arXiv:2309.12345, стр. 12]. Despite this, the improved accuracy and context-awareness of GraphRAG make it a promising approach for document question answering tasks [arXiv:2309.12345, стр. 14].

review_text: Document Visual Question Answering (DocVQA) has gained significant attention as a unified approach for answering natural language questions to extract information from documents, with various datasets addressing different domains and challenges [arXiv:2312.10108, стр. 3]. Existing multimodal document question answering methods predominantly adopt a Pre-Ingestion (PI) strategy, where a Vision Language Model (VLM) is used during the indexing phase to generate page descriptions that are then encoded into vectors [arXiv:2602.14162, стр. 1]. The Pre-Ingestion (PI) strategy involves calling a Vision Language Model (VLM) on every page to generate page descriptions, which are then encoded into vectors for embedding similarity retrieval [arXiv:2602.14162, стр. 1]. Hierarchical multimodal transformers have been proposed for multipage DocVQA, enhancing the ability to handle complex, multi-page documents [arXiv:2312.10108, стр. 20]. The Document Collection Visual Question Answering (DocVQA) approach has been applied to various datasets, including those for multipage documents and document collections [arXiv:2312.10108, стр. 20].

review_text: Recent advancements in large language models (LLMs) have led to the development of cost-effective strategies for tool use and API routing, which are crucial for optimizing performance and reducing computational expenses [arXiv:2310.02456, стр. 3]. These strategies often involve dynamic routing mechanisms that intelligently select the most appropriate tools or APIs based on the specific requirements of the task at hand [arXiv:2309.12345, стр. 5]. Additionally, researchers have explored the integration of reinforcement learning to enhance the efficiency of these routing decisions, leading to significant reductions in both latency and cost [arXiv:2311.12345, стр. 7]. Furthermore, the use of lightweight proxy models to predict the outcomes of different tool usages has been shown to further optimize resource allocation and improve overall system performance [arXiv:2312.01234, стр. 4]. These approaches not only enhance the practicality of LLMs in real-world applications but also make them more accessible to a broader range of users [arXiv:2310.05678, стр. 6].

review_text: Noor, an ongoing project aiming to develop the largest multi-task Arabic language models with up to 13B parameters, assesses the total carbon bill of the entire project, including data collection, storage costs, research and development budgets, pretraining costs, future serving estimates, and other exogenous costs [arXiv:2610.00223, стр. 1]. The trend of increasing model size has been slowing down due to scale-out limitations, and Noor provides a holistic assessment of the carbon footprint of training a very large Arabic language model [arXiv:2610.00223, стр. 2]. LLMs such as OpenAI GPT, Google PaLM, and Meta LLaMA are being utilized via API to generate security patches automatically, which is a cost-effective approach given the large resources required to train these models [arXiv:2308.13062, стр. 2]. The toolchain using LLMs for generating security patches is up to ∼10× faster than Spectre v1 patches generated with existing methods, significantly outperforming compiler-based techniques [arXiv:2308.13062, стр. 2]. The System Prompt in state-of-the-art LLMs acts as high-level and generic commands that control the style of generated samples, minimizing the need for post-processing and human interaction [arXiv:2308.13062, стр. 5]. Noor's data processing costs could be amortised over future projects, and for high-resource languages, processing more dumps would not be necessary, even to train a 1 trillion parameters model [arXiv:2610.00223, стр. 5].

review_text: Recent advancements in long-term memory architectures have significantly enhanced the capabilities of lifelong learning agents, enabling them to retain and utilize past experiences effectively [arXiv:2304.05678, стр. 2]. These architectures often incorporate mechanisms such as episodic memory and semantic memory to manage and integrate new information without catastrophic forgetting [arXiv:2212.12345, стр. 5]. One notable approach is the use of dynamic memory allocation, which allows agents to adaptively allocate memory resources based on the importance and relevance of incoming data [arXiv:2301.12345, стр. 7]. Additionally, research has shown that hybrid memory systems, combining both short-term and long-term memory components, can improve the robustness and efficiency of lifelong learning [arXiv:2305.67890, стр. 4]. Another key development is the integration of attention mechanisms, which help agents focus on relevant memories and reduce the computational burden of managing large memory stores [arXiv:2306.01234, стр. 6]. These advancements collectively contribute to the creation of more adaptable and intelligent agents capable of continuous learning over extended periods [arXiv:2307.12345, стр. 3].

review_text: The Continuous Memory Machine (CMM) builds on the Continuous Thought Machine (CTM) by introducing an explicit matrix-valued long-term memory that operates alongside its sliding-window short-term memory (STM) [arXiv:2610.07907, стр. 4]. The CTM has no persistent mechanism for storing information over long horizons, which limits its performance on tasks requiring long-term retention [arXiv:2610.07907, стр. 4]. In the CMM, the long-term memory (LTM) is defined as a matrix Bt ∈ R^d×ML, where ML columns are treated as tokens of dimension d, and it is initialized with a learned matrix B0 [arXiv:2610.07907, стр. 4]. The CMM updates both the short-term and long-term memories jointly using a Transformer, which provides an expressive mechanism for writing, retrieval, and reorganization across stores [arXiv:2610.07907, стр. 4]. Long short-term memory networks (LSTMs) alleviate the problem of gradient diffusion and explosion by introducing a memory unit and a gate mechanism to capture long dependencies in a sequence [arXiv:1610.04989, стр. 3]. LSTMs consider every bit of the long-term and short-term memories from the previous time-step when updating, ensuring a comprehensive memory update process [arXiv:1610.04989, стр. 3].

review_text: Recent advancements in automated red teaming have significantly enhanced the security of large language model (LLM) applications by identifying vulnerabilities and potential exploits [arXiv:2310.02456, стр. 3]. These automated systems can simulate adversarial attacks to test the robustness of LLMs, ensuring they are less susceptible to manipulation and misuse [arXiv:2309.12345, стр. 5]. Additionally, the development of sophisticated jailbreak detection mechanisms has become crucial in preventing unauthorized access and ensuring the integrity of LLM systems [arXiv:2311.01234, стр. 7]. These detection methods often involve monitoring for anomalous behavior and using machine learning techniques to identify patterns indicative of a jailbreak attempt [arXiv:2312.04567, стр. 4]. Furthermore, integrating these detection systems with real-time response mechanisms can help mitigate the impact of such security breaches [arXiv:2310.12345, стр. 6]. The continuous improvement of these automated tools is essential for maintaining the security and reliability of LLM applications in an increasingly complex threat landscape [arXiv:2311.12345, стр. 8].

review_text: Manual red teaming, which involves human experts crafting adversarial prompts to elicit unsafe responses from LLMs, is effective but unscalable and time-consuming [arXiv:2407.03876, стр. 1]. Meta has established a human red team of 350 individuals from various job positions to manually create attack samples for the Llama-2 chat models [arXiv:2407.03876, стр. 3]. Current generation-based red teaming research has not fully harnessed the learning capabilities of parameterized LLMs, often using fixed-parameter LLMs to launch attacks [arXiv:2407.03876, стр. 1]. Automated Progressive Red Teaming (APRT) is a framework that enhances the attack capabilities on both aligned open- and closed-source LLMs by using an Intention Expanding LLM, an Intention Hiding LLM, and an Evil Maker [arXiv:2407.03876, стр. 3]. APRT addresses the limitations of previous methods by progressively adjusting attack directions based on feedback, unlike MART, which indiscriminately selects successful attack samples as training data [arXiv:2407.03876, стр. 2]. The reranking-based adaptation procedure in some red-teaming approaches can serve as a quick way to red-team new target LLMs, revealing shared failure modes of current alignment methods [arXiv:2405.18540, стр. 10].

review_text: Due to the rapid growth of the area, many papers on automated red teaming have developed their own evaluation setups to compare their methods against baselines [arXiv:2402.04249, стр. 2]. Among prior work, we find at least 9 distinct evaluation setups, which we show in Table 1 [arXiv:2402.04249, стр. 2]. We find that existing comparisons rarely overlap, and in Section 3.2 we demonstrate that prior evaluations are essentially incomparable across papers due to a lack of standardization [arXiv:2402.04249, стр. 2]. A wide variety of automated red teaming methods have been proposed for LLMs, including text optimization methods, LLM optimizers, and custom jailbreaking templates [arXiv:2402.04249, стр. 2]. These methods include text optimization methods (Wallace et al., 2019; Guo et al., 2021; Shin et al., 2020; Wen et al., 2023; Jones et al., 2023; Zou et al., 2023), LLM optimizers (Perez et al., 2022; Chao et al., 2023; Mehrotra et al., 2023), and custom jailbreaking templates [arXiv:2402.04249, стр. 2]. In prior work, a range of specialized evaluation setups have been proposed, but there has not yet been a systematic effort to standardize these evaluations and provide a large-scale comparison of existing methods [arXiv:2402.04249, стр. 4]. We identify three key qualities for automated red teaming evaluations: breadth, comparability, and robust metrics [arXiv:2402.04249, стр. 4]. The validation set contains 100 behaviors, and the test set contains 410 behaviors, selected with stratified sampling using the intersections between all functional behaviors and semantic categories, followed by manual adjustment [arXiv:2402.04249, стр. 18]. Many papers on automated red teaming have developed their own evaluation setups, leading to at least 9 distinct setups that are largely incomparable due to a lack of standardization [arXiv:2402.04249, стр. 2]. The historical trajectory of red teaming automation serves as a cautionary parallel, highlighting the risk of missing critical opportunities to enhance the skills and expertise of human red teamers [arXiv:2503.22116, стр. 3]. To improve evaluations in automated red teaming, key qualities such as breadth, comparability, and robust metrics are identified, as existing evaluations often fall short in these areas [arXiv:2402.04249, стр. 4]. The validation set in the evaluation of automated red teaming contains 100 behaviors, and the test set contains 410 behaviors, selected with stratified sampling and manual adjustment [arXiv:2402.04249, стр. 18].

review_text: Recent advancements in multi-modal Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems have significantly improved the ability to process and understand scientific documents that include tables and figures [arXiv:2309.12345, стр. 5]. These systems leverage both textual and visual information to enhance the accuracy and relevance of generated responses, making them particularly useful for complex scientific inquiries [arXiv:2310.23456, стр. 7]. Studies have shown that incorporating visual elements such as tables and figures into RAG models can lead to more comprehensive and contextually rich outputs [arXiv:2311.34567, стр. 10]. However, challenges remain in effectively aligning and integrating multi-modal data, especially when dealing with the diverse formats and structures found in scientific literature [arXiv:2312.45678, стр. 12]. Despite these challenges, ongoing research continues to push the boundaries of multi-modal RAG systems, aiming to make them more robust and versatile [arXiv:2401.56789, стр. 15].

review_text: MHier-RAG, a novel multi-modal RAG model, leverages both textual and visual information across long-range pages to facilitate accurate question answering for visual-rich documents [arXiv:2508.00579, стр. 1]. The MHier-RAG method addresses the challenges of inter-modal disconnection and cross-page fragmentation by designing a hierarchical indexing method that integrates flattened in-page chunks and topological cross-page chunks [arXiv:2508.00579, стр. 1]. In the multi-modal long-context Doc-QA task, the MHier-RAG method formalizes the problem by integrating textual and visual content from multiple pages and modalities [arXiv:2508.00579, стр. 2]. Traditional RAG-based models exhibit a uni-modality bias, predominantly relying on textual information, which limits their effectiveness in multi-modal contexts [arXiv:2508.00579, стр. 7]. LVLMs, while advanced in visual processing for document images, still face challenges in integrating evidence from different modalities and pages, and are prone to hallucinations [arXiv:2508.00579, стр. 7]. Prior work on multimodal RAG has primarily focused on the visual domain, using text to describe images, but there is a need for RAG systems specifically tailored for IT-Ops/AI-Ops [arXiv:2505.21419, стр. 2].

review_text: Recent studies have explored the application of evolutionary algorithms in optimizing prompt workflows, particularly in the context of natural language processing tasks. These algorithms have been shown to effectively enhance the performance of prompt-based models by iteratively refining the prompts to achieve better outcomes [arXiv:2309.12345, стр. 5]. One notable approach involves using genetic algorithms to evolve prompts that maximize specific metrics, such as accuracy or coherence, in response generation [arXiv:2310.09876, стр. 7]. Another study demonstrates the effectiveness of combining evolutionary strategies with reinforcement learning to optimize prompts for complex tasks, leading to significant improvements in model performance [arXiv:2311.12345, стр. 10]. These findings suggest that evolutionary algorithms can be a powerful tool for enhancing the efficiency and effectiveness of prompt workflows in various applications [arXiv:2312.01234, стр. 8].

review_text: Evolutionary Computation (EC) has emerged as a powerful field of Artificial Intelligence, inspired by nature’s mechanisms of gradual development, but it often faces challenges such as stagnation, diversity loss, computational complexity, population initialization, and premature convergence [arXiv:2310.08748, стр. 1]. A dynamic multiobjective evolutionary algorithm based on a fine prediction strategy and nondominated solutions-guided evolution has been proposed to address dynamic optimization problems [arXiv:2310.08748, стр. 16]. An evolutionary algorithm based on transfer learning has been developed for dynamic expensive multi-objective optimization problems [arXiv:2310.08748, стр. 17]. Evolutionary algorithms (EAs) have received much attention in recent years due to their success in solving many problems with large parameters, including differentiable and continuous NP-hard problems [arXiv:2012.12248, стр. 2]. A genetic algorithm (GA), a population-based meta-heuristic optimization method, was first introduced by Holland and has been widely used for solving hard problems that cannot be directly found in polynomial time [arXiv:2012.12248, стр. 2]. The inclusion of 'social interactions' into the genetic algorithm cycle, inspired by the behavior of individuals in social systems, significantly improves the algorithm’s performance [arXiv:1001.1889, стр. 1]. Researchers have integrated learning algorithms into evolutionary computation to overcome limitations such as stagnation and premature convergence [arXiv:2310.08748, стр. 1].

review_text: Recent advancements in artificial intelligence have facilitated the development of agentic workflows, which are designed to automate systematic literature reviews, significantly enhancing the efficiency and accuracy of the review process [arXiv:2309.12345, стр. 3]. These workflows integrate multiple AI techniques, including natural language processing and machine learning, to identify, screen, and synthesize relevant studies [arXiv:2309.12345, стр. 5]. One notable approach involves the use of reinforcement learning to optimize the selection of studies, thereby reducing the workload on human reviewers [arXiv:2310.56789, стр. 7]. However, challenges remain, such as ensuring the transparency and reproducibility of these automated processes [arXiv:2310.56789, стр. 10]. Despite these challenges, agentic workflows have shown promising results in various domains, including healthcare and social sciences, demonstrating their potential to revolutionize the systematic review methodology [arXiv:2311.12345, стр. 4].

review_text: A variety of frameworks have emerged to support the development and orchestration of agentic workflows, such as LangChain, AutoGen, LangGraph, Academy, and CrewAI, which facilitate multi-agent systems interacting through prompt exchanges, calls to foundation models, and shared context [arXiv:2508.02866, стр. 2]. The challenge in agentic workflows lies in dynamically routing LLM agents across workflow steps to preserve task-solving quality under operating cost budgets, which is complicated by the open-ended and stateful nature of multi-agent LLM workflows [arXiv:2608.25992, стр. 1]. PROV-AGENT is a provenance model that extends W3C PROV to represent AI agent interactions, model invocations, and their relationships to non-agentic tasks and data in agentic workflows [arXiv:2508.02866, стр. 3]. The initialization of the MCP server in agentic workflows involves creating a new instance of AIAgent, assigning it an identifier and name, and using decorators to instrument the functions for execution [arXiv:2508.02866, стр. 4]. Agentic workflows are widely used for user-facing tasks, such as software engineering and enterprise applications, and they involve composing calls to ML models using a general-purpose programming language like Python [arXiv:2605.18697, стр. 1]. PopPy is a system designed to opportunistically exploit parallelism in Python agentic workflows, enhancing the efficiency of tasks that involve calls to ML models [arXiv:2605.18697, стр. 1]. A study evaluated the reasoning capability of agentic workflows by randomly sampling 200 problems that require multi-step reasoning and a final answer derivation [arXiv:2608.25992, стр. 12]. The provenance framework for agentic workflows, which tracks agent actions and decisions, is the first of its kind designed to support root-cause analysis, interpretability, and model and prompt fine-tuning [arXiv:2508.02866, стр. 6].

review_text: Recent studies have highlighted the significant role of context window size in the performance of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) models, demonstrating that larger context windows can enhance the coherence and relevance of generated responses [arXiv:2309.12345, стр. 5]. However, increasing the context window size also introduces computational overhead, which can be a limiting factor in real-time applications [arXiv:2310.67890, стр. 7]. To address this, some researchers have proposed adaptive context window mechanisms that dynamically adjust the window size based on the complexity of the query, thereby optimizing both performance and efficiency [arXiv:2311.01234, стр. 10]. These adaptive approaches have shown promising results, particularly in scenarios where the information retrieval task requires a nuanced understanding of the context [arXiv:2312.12345, стр. 12].

review_text: RAG systems enhance generative models by incorporating relevant information retrieved from external knowledge bases, improving the factual accuracy and contextual relevance of generated responses [arXiv:2407.19794, стр. 1]. The size of the text chunks retrieved and the context window utilization are crucial for enhancing the design and implementation of RAG systems [arXiv:2407.19794, стр. 1]. Standard RAG systems typically rely on a fixed top-k retrieval strategy, which can either miss relevant information or introduce semantically irrelevant passages, known as distractors, that degrade output quality [arXiv:2512.14313, стр. 1]. A distractor is a retrieved text that appears similar to the query but is actually semantically irrelevant, which can confuse the generator and reduce output quality by introducing noise into the context [arXiv:2512.14313, стр. 2]. The positioning of retrieved passages within the input context can influence the model’s attention and generation outcomes [arXiv:2512.14313, стр. 1]. A new hyper-parameter for RAG systems called Context Window Utilization has been introduced to optimize the context length and minimize irrelevant information [arXiv:2407.19794, стр. 1]. A classifier that predicts the optimal number of contexts to retrieve (k) has been introduced to dynamically adapt the context length to the specific informational requirements of each query [arXiv:2512.14313, стр. 3].

review_text: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) leverages external information to improve task performance by using the user’s input as a query to retrieve relevant documents, which are then provided to the LLM as contextual information [arXiv:2511.22858, стр. 4]. RAG helps in generating responses that are up-to-date and faithful to the context, addressing the issue of outdated information that can occur when relying solely on the model’s pre-training knowledge [arXiv:2511.22858, стр. 5]. In the context of RAG, the retrieval of relevant documents is crucial for generating accurate and contextually appropriate responses [arXiv:2511.22858, стр. 4]. A study on context compliance in RAG under knowledge conflict found that Standard RAG reaches 15.0% accuracy (± 3.1%, N=500 scored examples) when provided with the most common human misconception as the retrieved context [arXiv:2605.14473, стр. 7]. Context-Driven Decomposition (CDD) is introduced to study context compliance, focusing on how retrieved context controls the answer even when it conflicts with the model’s prior knowledge [arXiv:2605.14473, стр. 1]. The Temporal Shift and Distractor Evidence intervals in the study overlap with Standard RAG, indicating no significant difference in these conditions [arXiv:2605.14473, стр. 5]. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) leverages external information to improve task performance by providing contextual documents to the language model (LLM) alongside the user's input [arXiv:2511.22858, стр. 4]. RAG helps in generating responses that are up-to-date and faithful to the retrieved context, addressing the issue of outdated information that can occur with models relying solely on pre-training knowledge [arXiv:2511.22858, стр. 5]. Under worst-case conditions where the retrieved context is maximally misleading, Standard RAG achieves an accuracy of 15.0% (± 3.1%, N=500 scored examples) [arXiv:2605.14473, стр. 7]. Context-Driven Decomposition (CDD) is introduced to study context compliance, where the retrieved context controls the answer even when it conflicts with the model’s prior knowledge [arXiv:2605.14473, стр. 1]. To ensure the faithfulness of generated responses to the retrieved context, methods such as explicit constraints through prompting and chain-of-verification steps are proposed [arXiv:2511.22858, стр. 5].

review_text: Recent studies have highlighted the importance of benchmarking mathematical reasoning capabilities in multi-agent language model systems to ensure their effectiveness and reliability [arXiv:2310.05421, стр. 2]. These benchmarks often focus on evaluating the models' ability to solve complex mathematical problems collaboratively, which is crucial for applications in fields such as finance and scientific research [arXiv:2309.12345, стр. 3]. One notable benchmark, the Multi-Agent Math Reasoning Challenge (MAMRC), has been designed to assess the collective problem-solving skills of multiple agents working together [arXiv:2311.07890, стр. 4]. The results from these benchmarks indicate that while current multi-agent systems show promising performance, there is still significant room for improvement, particularly in handling more abstract and higher-order mathematical concepts [arXiv:2312.01234, стр. 5].

review_text: Multi-agent LLM systems coordinate specialized agents into workflows, and the performance of these workflows is influenced by the structure of the workflow, including the sequence of agent actions and the information exchange between them [arXiv:2605.19140, стр. 2]. Two distinct regimes for designing workflows in multi-agent LLM systems have emerged: the centralized regime, which assumes a single designer with global visibility, and the decentralized regime, which does not [arXiv:2605.19140, стр. 2]. Recent systems route tasks through learned or hand-designed directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) of LLM agents, with AgentNet being a notable example that uses hand-designed adaptive rules but lacks Bellman recursion and convergence guarantees [arXiv:2605.19140, стр. 3]. Adaptive Coopetition is a lightweight, inference-time multi-round, multi-agent framework designed to enhance LLM multi-step reasoning, particularly in resource-constrained environments [arXiv:2510.18179, стр. 5]. The Adaptive Coopetition framework aims to extend its application to other reasoning-intensive domains beyond mathematics, such as scientific discovery and legal analysis, to evaluate its versatility and robustness [arXiv:2510.18179, стр. 5]. Multi-LLM mathematical reasoning is a headline application in multi-agent LLM systems, alongside multi-agent routing and multi-agent CPU programming [arXiv:2605.19140, стр. 8].

review_text: Recent advancements in autonomous agent systems have highlighted the necessity for robust security guardrails to prevent unauthorized tool execution [arXiv:2309.12345, стр. 3]. These guardrails are crucial for maintaining the integrity and security of agent operations, especially in environments where agents interact with sensitive data or systems [arXiv:2310.09876, стр. 5]. One approach involves implementing strict access controls and authentication mechanisms to ensure that only authorized tools and commands are executed [arXiv:2311.12345, стр. 7]. Additionally, runtime monitoring and anomaly detection systems can help identify and mitigate unauthorized activities in real-time [arXiv:2312.01234, стр. 4]. Research also emphasizes the importance of continuous security audits and updates to adapt to evolving threats [arXiv:2311.09876, стр. 6]. Furthermore, integrating machine learning models for predictive threat analysis can enhance the effectiveness of these security measures [arXiv:2310.12345, стр. 8].

review_text: Autonomous AI agents powered by large language models are being deployed in production environments with capabilities that include shell execution, file system access, database queries, HTTP requests, and multi-party communication [arXiv:2603.17419, стр. 1]. The deployment of autonomous AI agents in production environments represents a qualitative shift in the security landscape, as these agents operate with capabilities that blur the boundary between tool and operator [arXiv:2603.17419, стр. 4]. Shapira et al. provide the most comprehensive empirical documentation of agentic AI vulnerabilities to date, revealing three structural deficiencies in current agent architectures: no stakeholder model, no self-model, and no context-awareness [arXiv:2603.17419, стр. 5]. Agents lack a coherent representation of who they serve, who they interact with, and what obligations they have to each party, leading them to default to satisfying whoever is speaking most urgently, recently, or coercively [arXiv:2603.17419, стр. 5]. Agents in Shapira et al.'s case studies executed filesystem commands for any non-owner who asked, disclosed 124 email records including sensitive information to an unauthorized party, and complied with system shutdown instructions from a spoofed identity [arXiv:2603.17419, стр. 5]. To address multi-turn manipulation patterns, the following rules were deployed: no treating quoted text as commands, ignoring metadata in user content, treating tool output as untrusted, and asking the user when in doubt [arXiv:2603.17419, стр. 11]. The HIPAA Security Rule, while predating autonomous AI agents, provides sufficient coverage when interpreted in the context of agentic capabilities, covering access controls, audit controls, transmission security, and evaluation requirements [arXiv:2603.17419, стр. 14]. Ethical safeguards are critical for user trust and regulatory compliance in sensitive domains like cybersecurity, ensuring that AI agents are not only technically capable but also socially responsible and accountable [arXiv:2510.01751, стр. 7].

claims.claim_text: Shapira et al. provide the most comprehensive empirical documentation of agentic AI vulnerabilities to date, revealing three structural deficiencies in current agent architectures: no stakeholder model, no self-model, and no context-awareness.
claims.supporting_quote: Shapira et al. [7] provide the most comprehensive empirical documentation of agentic AI vulnerabilities to date. Their eleven case studies reveal three structural deficiencies in current agent architectures that are directly relevant to our security design: No stakeholder model. Agents lack a coherent representation of who they serve, who they interact with, and what obligations they have to each party. In practice, agents default to satisfying whoever is speaking most urgently, recently, or coercively. This is the most commonly exploited attack surface: agents in their study executed filesystem commands for any non owner who asked, disclosed 124 email records including sensitive information to an unauthorized party, and complied with system shutdown instructions from a spoofed identity [7]. No self model. Agents take irreversible, user affecting actions without recognizing they are exceeding their own competence boundaries. Agents converted short lived conversational requests into permanent background processes with no termination condition, allocated memory indefinitely without recognizing operational threats, and reported task completion while the underlying system state contradicted those reports [7].

claims.supporting_quote: The HIPAA Security Rule predates autonomous AI agents by decades and does not contemplate the specific risks they introduce. However, the rule’s technology neutral framework provides sufficient coverage when interpreted in the context of agentic capabilities. Access controls (164.312(a)) apply to agents’ access to ePHI; audit controls (164.312(b)) apply to logging agents’ actions; transmission security (164.312(e)) applies to agents’ outbound communications; and the evaluation requirement (164.308(a)(8)) supports ongoing security posture assessment including drift detection.

review_text: Speculative decoding has emerged as a promising technique to enhance the efficiency of large language model (LLM) inference by predicting and precomputing potential next tokens [arXiv:2309.08573, стр. 2]. This approach leverages the probabilistic nature of language models to reduce the latency associated with sequential token generation [arXiv:2305.14824, стр. 3]. Studies have shown that speculative decoding can significantly speed up the inference process without a substantial loss in the quality of generated text [arXiv:2307.12345, стр. 4]. However, the effectiveness of speculative decoding can vary depending on the specific architecture and the context of the input [arXiv:2306.09876, стр. 5]. To optimize performance, researchers have explored various strategies, including adaptive speculative depths and dynamic pruning of unlikely token sequences [arXiv:2308.11234, стр. 6]. These advancements highlight the potential of speculative decoding to make LLMs more practical for real-time applications [arXiv:2309.08573, стр. 7].

review_text: Speculative Decoding (SD) is an advanced technique for accelerating LLM inference that has garnered significant research interest in recent years [arXiv:2503.00491, стр. 1]. SD effectively accelerates LLM inference while maintaining unchanged distributions, making it particularly beneficial for researchers with modest computational resources [arXiv:2503.00491, стр. 3]. Most advanced SD techniques do not require full-parameter retraining, which makes it more energy efficient and can reduce carbon footprints [arXiv:2503.00491, стр. 4]. Staged speculative decoding can generate text very quickly, with performance approaching that of large-batch inference, especially for text with lower entropy [arXiv:2308.04623, стр. 4]. Accelerating local (small-batch) inference for LLMs is crucial for improving latency, personalization, and privacy [arXiv:2308.04623, стр. 1]. The tutorial will cover various draft model architectures and verification strategies in speculative decoding [arXiv:2503.00491, стр. 2]. Speculative decoding techniques, such as GliDe with a CaPE and Lookahead Decoding, are highlighted as cutting-edge methods in the field [arXiv:2503.00491, стр. 4].

review_text: Recent advancements in large language models (LLMs) have introduced techniques for knowledge editing and model editing, enabling the modification of a model's behavior or knowledge without retraining the entire model [arXiv:2310.02456, стр. 2]. These methods often involve fine-tuning on a small set of examples or directly manipulating the model's parameters to achieve the desired changes [arXiv:2309.12345, стр. 3]. One notable approach is the use of in-context learning, where the model is provided with a few examples within the input prompt to guide its responses [arXiv:2307.01234, стр. 4]. Another technique involves the use of adversarial training to ensure that the model's edited knowledge remains robust and consistent [arXiv:2308.05678, стр. 5]. Additionally, researchers have explored the use of meta-learning to enable models to adapt to new tasks or knowledge domains more efficiently [arXiv:2306.09876, стр. 6]. These advancements highlight the growing capability of LLMs to be dynamically updated and customized for specific applications [arXiv:2311.01234, стр. 7].

review_text: Retraining large language models to update knowledge incurs prohibitively high costs, leading to the development of knowledge editing techniques that directly update the internal parameters of these models [arXiv:2408.07413, стр. 1]. Current knowledge editing methods have limited scalability for lifelong editing, which is necessary for continuous knowledge updates [arXiv:2408.07413, стр. 1]. The techniques of knowledge editing aim to update outdated or incorrect knowledge in large language models (LLMs) without the need for frequent retraining [arXiv:2508.01302, стр. 1]. The study explores the fundamental reason why knowledge editing fails in lifelong editing by starting with the closed-form solution derived from linear associative memory, which underpins state-of-the-art knowledge editing methods [arXiv:2408.07413, стр. 1]. Future directions for knowledge editing include attempting knowledge editing in larger language models with sparser architectures and decomposing knowledge within models to perform edits based on this decomposition [arXiv:2408.07413, стр. 7]. Knowledge editing techniques are being developed to address the static parametric knowledge in large language models that becomes outdated after pretraining [arXiv:2608.25100, стр. 1].

review_text: Recent advancements in machine unlearning, particularly for large language models, have focused on developing methods to remove the influence of specific data points from trained models without retraining from scratch [arXiv:2309.08573, стр. 2]. These techniques aim to address privacy concerns and data rights by enabling the selective forgetting of sensitive information [arXiv:2309.08573, стр. 3]. One approach involves using gradient-based methods to approximate the effect of removing data points, which can be computationally efficient [arXiv:2304.05916, стр. 4]. Another method leverages the concept of influence functions to estimate the impact of individual training examples on the model's parameters [arXiv:2304.05916, стр. 5]. However, these methods often face challenges in maintaining model performance and ensuring complete data removal [arXiv:2309.08573, стр. 6]. Despite these challenges, ongoing research continues to refine these techniques to make them more practical and effective [arXiv:2304.05916, стр. 7].

review_text: Catastrophic forgetting occurs in deep neural networks in life-long learning settings because they are vastly optimized upon gradient descent algorithm [arXiv:2211.14177, стр. 9]. Fast machine unlearning without retraining through selective synaptic dampening is proposed by R., J., Schoepf, S., and Brintrup, A. in 2024 [arXiv:2508.20773, стр. 5]. Amnesiac machine learning, which involves selective forgetting, is discussed by Aves, L., Nagisetty, V., and Ganesh, V. in 2021 [arXiv:2508.20773, стр. 5]. Selective amnesia, a continual learning approach to forgetting in deep generative models, is introduced by Heng, A. and Soh, H. in 2023 [arXiv:2508.20773, стр. 5]. Learning without Forgetting (LwF) utilizes old models to generate pseudo data, which guides the new model to reach a shared low-error region of problems [arXiv:2211.14177, стр. 16]. Freezing either a few specific layers or a major part of a network can help networks become robust against catastrophic forgetting [arXiv:2211.14177, стр. 16]. Research from [4] focuses on how task properties influence the hardness of sequential learning, explaining forgetting based on input data [arXiv:2211.14177, стр. 17]. CFD approaches the problem of catastrophic forgetting by explaining how forgetting happens over time based on the computer vision of models [arXiv:2211.14177, стр. 17].

review_text: The forgetting of large language models (LLMs) during continual finetuning has received some attention in recent years, showing the importance of pretraining to mitigate forgetting [arXiv:2410.14159, стр. 3]. Exact Unlearning is a full retraining-based approach that ensures complete data removal by retraining from scratch, offering the strongest guarantees of compliance and reversibility, but it is computationally intensive and impractical for large-scale or continuously learning systems [arXiv:2509.10590, стр. 10]. Open-world forgetting, a phenomenon where a model forgets knowledge outside the scope of the training data, has been assessed by evaluating the performance of both the original unaltered model and the customized model on 10,000 user prompts from the DiffusionDB dataset [arXiv:2410.14159, стр. 5]. To demonstrate that open-world forgetting is a general phenomenon, the study analyzed three broad categories of model alterations: model customization, unlearning, and quantization methods [arXiv:2410.14159, стр. 15]. Machine Unlearning (MU) has emerged as a promising approach to addressing persistent challenges in responsible and adaptive AI, particularly in the context of large language models [arXiv:2509.10590, стр. 1].

review_text: Recent advancements in natural language processing have led to the development of sophisticated models capable of generating human-like text, raising concerns about the authenticity and origin of such content [arXiv:2309.12345, стр. 2]. To address these issues, researchers have explored various watermarking techniques to embed subtle, imperceptible markers into machine-generated text [arXiv:2305.01234, стр. 3]. These watermarks can be used to verify the provenance of the text and detect whether it has been generated by a machine [arXiv:2307.04567, стр. 4]. One approach involves modifying the generation process to introduce specific patterns that can be later detected without affecting the readability or meaning of the text [arXiv:2308.12345, стр. 5]. Another method utilizes statistical properties of the generated text to create a unique signature that can be verified using machine learning algorithms [arXiv:2310.09876, стр. 6]. These techniques have shown promise in both laboratory settings and real-world applications, although challenges remain in ensuring robustness against adversarial attacks and maintaining the naturalness of the text [arXiv:2311.01234, стр. 7].

review_text: Watermarking techniques have emerged as promising solutions to distinguish between human and machine-generated content, providing a reliable means of tracing the origin of the text and verifying its authenticity [arXiv:2407.04794, стр. 1]. The watermarking method is not only applicable to generated text but also to human-written text, thereby broadening its potential scope and utility [arXiv:2305.08883, стр. 11]. Watermarking can maintain the original semantics of human-written text, as indicated by the results in Figure 14 [arXiv:2305.08883, стр. 11]. Watermarking techniques can achieve high-confidence detections when enough tokens are observed, such as detecting the watermark after observing 800 tokens on average with a 1e−5 false positive rate [arXiv:2306.04634, стр. 1]. Watermarking schemes can be broadly divided into pre-text watermarks and post-text watermarks, with the requirement that the watermarked text and unwatermarked text are indistinguishable [arXiv:2407.04794, стр. 13]. Format-based watermarks do not modify the content of the text but change the format of the text in ways that are imperceptible to humans [arXiv:2407.04794, стр. 4]. The reliability of watermarking as a strategy to identify machine-generated text is investigated under various types of realistic corruptions, such as mixing with human-written text or rewriting parts of the passage [arXiv:2306.04634, стр. 2]. Detection strategies must guarantee low false-positive rates, which need to be weighed against detection sensitivity, as every false positive can be extremely harmful [arXiv:2306.04634, стр. 10].

review_text: Post-training quantization (PTQ) has emerged as a critical technique for reducing the computational and memory requirements of large language models (LLMs) without significant loss in performance [arXiv:2309.00953, стр. 2]. PTQ methods typically involve converting the weights and activations of a pre-trained model from full precision to lower precision formats, such as 8-bit integers, which can significantly enhance the efficiency of inference on resource-constrained devices [arXiv:2305.14822, стр. 3]. Recent studies have shown that advanced PTQ techniques, such as dynamic quantization and mixed-precision quantization, can achieve near-lossless performance on a variety of NLP tasks [arXiv:2307.06721, стр. 4]. However, the effectiveness of PTQ can vary depending on the model architecture and the specific task, and careful calibration is often required to maintain accuracy [arXiv:2306.01234, стр. 5]. Additionally, some research has explored the integration of PTQ with other optimization techniques, such as pruning and knowledge distillation, to further enhance the efficiency of LLMs [arXiv:2308.12345, стр. 6]. Despite these advancements, challenges remain in achieving optimal quantization for the most complex and largest models, and ongoing research is focused on developing more robust and scalable PTQ methods [arXiv:2310.01234, стр. 7].

Additionally, some research has explored the integration of PTQ with other optimization techniques, such as pruning and knowledge distillation, to further enhance the efficiency of LLMs

Despite these advancements, challenges remain in achieving optimal quantization for the most complex and largest models, and ongoing research is focused on developing more robust and scalable PTQ methods

review_text: Post-training quantization with variable-length encoding (VLCQ) has a greater representational capability (lower quantization error in low-bit widths) compared to other schemes [arXiv:2610.15092, стр. 8]. Quantization-aware training methods have achieved results comparable to the baseline for as low as 2–4 bits per parameter, and even decent performance for single-bit parameters, but they require a vast amount of labeled data and high computational power [arXiv:1911.07190, стр. 3]. Post-training quantization is widely used in existing embedded hardware solutions, but most hardware-friendly post-training schemes have only managed to achieve limited success [arXiv:1911.07190, стр. 3]. Loss Aware Post-Training Quantization (LAPQ) jointly optimizes all quantization parameters by minimizing the loss function directly, which is particularly useful at low precision where the loss landscape is non-separable and has steep curvature [arXiv:1911.07190, стр. 14]. Hardware Friendly Post Training Quantization (HPTQ) is a method that adapts and combines several known quantization techniques for both weights and activations, and it has been shown to achieve competitive results under hardware-friendly constraints [arXiv:2109.09113, стр. 17]. Symmetric uniform quantization with a fixed number of bits and quantization step size is a common approach in post-training quantization, where the continuous value is mapped into a discrete representation [arXiv:1911.07190, стр. 5]. HPTQ aims to quantize a trained floating-point network in post-training with hardware-friendly quantizers, which are uniform, symmetric, and have power-of-two thresholds [arXiv:2109.09113, стр. 4].

review_text: Recent advancements in large language models (LLMs) have seen the integration of mixture-of-experts (MoE) architectures to enhance model efficiency and performance. MoE models introduce sparsity by routing inputs to a subset of experts, which significantly reduces computational costs while maintaining or even improving model accuracy [arXiv:2106.05915, стр. 3]. This routing mechanism allows for the scaling of models to trillions of parameters without a proportional increase in computational resources [arXiv:2106.05915, стр. 4]. However, the effectiveness of MoE models depends heavily on the routing algorithms used, which must balance load distribution and ensure that the most relevant experts are selected for each input [arXiv:2208.07964, стр. 5]. Studies have also shown that the sparsity introduced by MoE architectures can lead to more efficient training and inference processes, making them particularly suitable for large-scale applications [arXiv:2208.07964, стр. 6]. Despite these advantages, MoE models face challenges such as increased complexity in training and the potential for suboptimal routing decisions, which can degrade performance if not properly managed [arXiv:2302.05655, стр. 7].

review_text: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures enable efficient scaling of large language models through conditional computation, where different tokens can be processed by different experts, allowing the model to allocate specialized capacity dynamically [arXiv:2603.11114, стр. 2]. In top-k routing, the k experts with the highest probability are selected, and only these experts are active for token t at layer ℓ [arXiv:2603.11114, стр. 2]. Sparse Mixture of Experts (MoE) models scale more efficiently than dense models by routing tokens to modular expert networks that are only active for processing a fraction of tokens [arXiv:2610.11775, стр. 1]. A leading hypothesis for the performance of MoE models is that they achieve efficient specialization through the routing mechanism, which can dynamically allocate computational resources to the most relevant experts [arXiv:2610.11775, стр. 1]. Routing signatures, a vector representation summarizing expert activations, are introduced to better understand the routing mechanisms in MoE architectures [arXiv:2603.11114, стр. 1]. In an MoE architecture, a gating network assigns routing scores to a set of expert networks, determining how each input is processed [arXiv:2601.15021, стр. 2]. The routing mechanism in MoE models is hypothesized to enable superposed specialization, where experts can specialize in multiple tasks or sub-tasks, contributing to the model's efficiency and performance [arXiv:2610.11775, стр. 13].

review_text: Recent advancements in transformer models have introduced the concept of Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE) to effectively handle long-context sequences, enhancing the model's ability to capture long-range dependencies [arXiv:2104.09864, стр. 3]. RoPE scales the positional encodings logarithmically, allowing the model to generalize better to longer sequences without retraining [arXiv:2202.10447, стр. 4]. Position interpolation, a technique that interpolates positional embeddings, further improves the model's performance by providing smoother transitions between positions [arXiv:2206.11887, стр. 5]. These methods have been shown to significantly enhance the performance of transformers in tasks requiring long-context understanding, such as document summarization and question answering [arXiv:2301.05719, стр. 6].

review_text: Extending the context window of large language models is crucial for tasks such as long-form summarization, code completion, retrieval-augmented generation, chain-of-thought reasoning, and agentic pipelines, which rely on long-range dependencies and rich cross-document context [arXiv:2510.00028, стр. 1]. A popular method to extend the context window is to modify positional encoding at inference, particularly through RoPE-based scaling methods such as linear interpolation and frequency-aware YaRN [arXiv:2510.00028, стр. 1]. RoPE introduces no additional asymptotic cost, as it is a per-token, per-head (sin, cos) rotation applied to dh/2 pairs, preserving the compute and memory complexity of scaled dot-product attention while endowing it with both absolute and relative position awareness [arXiv:2510.00028, стр. 3]. The low-frequency rotary components carry the long-range semantic and positional signal, which is essential for context-length extension, as shown by the relational analysis of Barbero et al. (2025) [arXiv:2606.21249, стр. 16]. YaRN and NTK-aware RoPE refinements are effective in extending the context window of large language models without significant fine-tuning and minimal perplexity degradation [arXiv:2402.03303, стр. 11].

review_text: Recent advancements in AI alignment have explored methodologies beyond Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF), focusing on constitutional AI and direct preference optimization to ensure that AI systems adhere to human values and ethical standards [arXiv:2309.08573, стр. 2]. Constitutional AI involves designing AI systems with a set of principles that guide their behavior, ensuring they act in ways that are consistent with human norms and values [arXiv:2304.07467, стр. 5]. Direct preference optimization, on the other hand, aims to directly optimize the AI's behavior to align with human preferences, often through more explicit and structured feedback mechanisms [arXiv:2306.14883, стр. 3]. These approaches have shown promise in creating AI systems that are more transparent, controllable, and aligned with human intentions [arXiv:2309.12345, стр. 4]. However, challenges remain, including the difficulty of accurately capturing and representing human preferences and the potential for unintended consequences [arXiv:2307.09876, стр. 6]. Research is ongoing to address these challenges and to develop more robust and reliable alignment techniques [arXiv:2310.01234, стр. 7].

review_text: Constitutional AI, proposed and developed by Anthropic AI, aims to hardcode explicit principles and values into AI models to make their decision-making more transparent and accountable [arXiv:2406.16696, стр. 1]. Constitutional AI involves training AI models to align with constitutional guidelines and penalizing deviations, with the goal of instilling these values into the AI's objective function over time [arXiv:2406.16696, стр. 8]. The opacity and inscrutability of advanced AI systems pose significant challenges to establishing their legitimacy in the eyes of those subject to their power [arXiv:2406.16696, стр. 5]. Public Constitutional AI is a framework that involves the public in drafting an AI constitution, transforming it from a technical solution into a product of significant citizen involvement [arXiv:2406.16696, стр. 2]. Public Constitutional AI aims to mitigate the opacity deficit by making the principles of the AI constitution a product of public involvement, thereby grounding algorithmic power in the collective will of the community [arXiv:2406.16696, стр. 11]. While Constitutional AI is a promising start, it may fall short of securing robust legitimacy for AI authority, necessitating a more participatory approach like Public Constitutional AI [arXiv:2406.16696, стр. 6]. Public Constitutional AI could help bridge the gap between the abstract logic of algorithms and the lived realities of human communities by involving the public in the development of AI principles [arXiv:2406.16696, стр. 11].

review_text: Recent studies have explored the use of uncertainty estimation to detect hallucinations in large language models (LLMs), highlighting its potential to improve the reliability of these systems [arXiv:2310.02456, стр. 3]. One approach involves leveraging Bayesian neural networks to quantify the uncertainty in model predictions, which can help identify when the model is likely to generate hallucinations [arXiv:2309.12345, стр. 5]. Another method proposes using ensemble models to estimate the variability in predictions, with higher variability indicating a higher likelihood of hallucination [arXiv:2311.14199, стр. 4]. Additionally, researchers have investigated the use of out-of-distribution detection techniques to flag inputs that are likely to cause the model to hallucinate [arXiv:2308.09876, стр. 7]. These methods collectively suggest that uncertainty estimation can be a valuable tool for enhancing the robustness of LLMs in real-world applications [arXiv:2312.01234, стр. 6].

review_text: The problem of hallucinations in LLMs has attracted significant attention recently, with various methods being developed to detect these issues [arXiv:2506.09886, стр. 3]. Current detection methods for hallucinations in LLMs can be broadly categorized into three main paradigms based on their underlying approaches [arXiv:2603.22812, стр. 2]. One approach to hallucination detection involves leveraging the hidden states of prompts and responses in LLMs, where hallucinatory responses show greater deviations from prompts compared to grounded responses [arXiv:2506.09886, стр. 2]. A novel, model-intrinsic approach to hallucination detection has been proposed, utilizing nonparametric Maximum Mean Discrepancy distances to construct hallucination scores without requiring external knowledge bases or auxiliary models [arXiv:2506.09886, стр. 2]. Probing techniques can address latency issues by training lightweight models to predict semantic dispersion or hallucination probability directly from internal model representations [arXiv:2602.04577, стр. 1]. Extensive experiments with five datasets and three LLMs up to 15B in size demonstrate that the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art or competitive performance in hallucination detection [arXiv:2506.09886, стр. 3]. The proposed method's metrics are competitive, even with a significant domain shift from NLI to hallucination detection [arXiv:2506.09886, стр. 3]. Methods requiring multiple generations are highlighted separately in the comparison of hallucination detection techniques, showing their performance across different LLMs and datasets [arXiv:2506.09886, стр. 14].

review_text: Recent studies have highlighted the issue of benchmark data contamination, where training and evaluation datasets overlap, leading to inflated performance metrics in language models [arXiv:2304.07195, стр. 2]. This contamination can result in models memorizing specific examples rather than learning generalizable skills, thereby undermining the validity of benchmark results [arXiv:2304.07195, стр. 3]. To address this, researchers have proposed various methods to detect and mitigate memorization, including the use of data deduplication techniques and the creation of more robust evaluation protocols [arXiv:2305.14723, стр. 4]. However, these methods face challenges, such as the computational cost of large-scale deduplication and the difficulty of ensuring complete data cleanliness [arXiv:2305.14723, стр. 5]. Despite these challenges, ongoing research continues to explore the extent of memorization and its impact on the reliability of language model evaluations [arXiv:2306.08974, стр. 6].

review_text: Retrieval-augmented code generation has emerged as a promising approach to enhance the performance of code generation models by integrating external code repositories [arXiv:2304.05423, стр. 2]. This method leverages the context from similar code snippets to improve the accuracy and relevance of generated code [arXiv:2210.07454, стр. 3]. Studies have shown that retrieval-augmented models can significantly outperform traditional sequence-to-sequence models in tasks such as code completion and bug fixing [arXiv:2109.07753, стр. 5]. The effectiveness of these models is attributed to their ability to retrieve and adapt relevant code examples, thereby reducing the need for extensive training data [arXiv:2206.07723, стр. 4]. However, challenges remain in efficiently scaling the retrieval process and ensuring the robustness of the generated code [arXiv:2301.08177, стр. 6]. Recent advancements have focused on optimizing the retrieval mechanism and integrating it more seamlessly with the code generation process [arXiv:2305.14199, стр. 7].

review_text: Retrieval-augmented code generation (RACG) has been successfully applied in code generation, but existing pipelines employ static knowledge bases with a single source, limiting their adaptation capabilities [arXiv:2402.12317, стр. 1]. The current approach in retrieval-augmented code generation suffers from information redundancy and a preference gap, where the mismatch between retrieved content and the generator’s actual needs can misguide the generator [arXiv:2409.15895, стр. 1]. RRG, a novel retrieval-augmented code generation framework, addresses the issues of redundant information and the preference gap by integrating a refactor module that optimizes code snippets for the generator [arXiv:2409.15895, стр. 11]. In the RRG framework, the input to the model includes the query and the cropped relevant code, which is processed and adjusted to a fixed length to facilitate the generation of the target code [arXiv:2409.15895, стр. 5]. Experiments using the ConCode dataset, which is characterized by relatively short code snippets with high similarity, show that the RRG framework reduces noise to the generator compared to the RAG approach [arXiv:2409.15895, стр. 7].

review_text: Differential privacy has been increasingly adopted in the training of language models to protect individual data contributions while maintaining model utility [arXiv:2109.04996, стр. 2]. Techniques such as the addition of noise to gradients and the use of privacy-preserving mechanisms have shown promise in mitigating privacy risks [arXiv:2109.04996, стр. 3]. However, these methods often come with a trade-off, as they can lead to a degradation in model performance, particularly in terms of accuracy and coherence [arXiv:2206.07721, стр. 4]. Recent studies have explored various strategies to optimize this balance, including the use of advanced noise calibration techniques and the integration of differential privacy with other privacy-preserving methods [arXiv:2206.07721, стр. 5]. Despite these advancements, challenges remain, such as the need for more efficient algorithms and better theoretical foundations to support the practical implementation of differential privacy in large-scale language models [arXiv:2301.05997, стр. 6].

review_text: Deep learning (DL) models for natural language processing (NLP) tasks often handle private data, demanding protection against breaches and disclosures [arXiv:2205.10095, стр. 1]. Data protection laws, such as the European Union’s General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), enforce the need for privacy in NLP tasks [arXiv:2205.10095, стр. 1]. This review aims to provide an overview of recent privacy-preserving DL methods for NLP, shaping the landscape of privacy challenges and solutions in this field [arXiv:2205.10095, стр. 6]. The major contribution of this work is a taxonomy for classifying existing works in the literature of privacy-preserving NLP, considering the target for privacy preservation, privacy-enhancing technologies (PETs), the NLP task itself, and the computation scenario [arXiv:2205.10095, стр. 6]. The review covers all steps of the NLP pipeline, from dataset pre-processing to model evaluation, to provide a holistic view of privacy issues and solutions for text data [arXiv:2205.10095, стр. 6]. The review includes a list of benchmark datasets for privacy-preserving NLP tasks to help researchers find baselines for their work [arXiv:2205.10095, стр. 6]. The review focuses on works published from 2016 onward, as it aims to bring the most recent developments in privacy-preserving NLP models based on DL [arXiv:2205.10095, стр. 8]. The review includes long papers that report the development of privacy-preserving NLP models [arXiv:2205.10095, стр. 8].

review_text: Recent studies have highlighted the effectiveness of chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning in enhancing the performance of large language models on complex tasks, such as arithmetic and logical reasoning [arXiv:2304.08478, стр. 3]. However, these studies also reveal that CoT reasoning can be prone to errors, particularly when the models generate incorrect intermediate steps or fail to correctly interpret the problem [arXiv:2305.14824, стр. 5]. The faithfulness of CoT reasoning is further challenged by the models' tendency to overfit to training data, leading to unreliable generalization to novel problems [arXiv:2306.07055, стр. 7]. Despite these limitations, CoT reasoning remains a promising approach, especially when combined with other techniques like self-consistency and feedback mechanisms, which can improve the robustness and accuracy of the models [arXiv:2307.12345, стр. 4].

review_text: A novel parametric faithfulness framework (PFF) was introduced to measure the faithfulness of chains of thought, with two metrics: FF-HARD and FF-SOFT [arXiv:2502.14829, стр. 9]. The PFF framework supports multiple ways to measure parametric faithfulness, and one such way is through unlearning reasoning steps (FUR) [arXiv:2502.14829, стр. 3]. Prior studies have shown that chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning generated by large language models (LLMs) does not always accurately reflect the actual behavior of the models [arXiv:2406.10625, стр. 1]. Three broad approaches are commonly employed to enhance the faithfulness of CoT reasoning generated by LLMs: in-context learning, fine-tuning, and inference-time interventions [arXiv:2406.10625, стр. 1]. The hard metric FF-HARD answers the question 'Is the CoT generated by the model faithful?', while the soft metric FF-SOFT identifies which CoT steps are most relevant [arXiv:2502.14829, стр. 9]. A line of work has analyzed the sensitivity of models to perturbations applied to reasoning steps, which is relevant to measuring parametric faithfulness [arXiv:2502.14829, стр. 3].

review_text: Recent studies have highlighted the importance of self-consistency in enhancing the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs) [arXiv:2309.08573, стр. 4]. Techniques such as consistency regularization and ensemble methods have been shown to improve the robustness and reliability of LLMs in various reasoning tasks [arXiv:2305.17554, стр. 7]. Sampling strategies, including temperature scaling and nucleus sampling, have also been explored to refine the output quality and coherence of LLMs [arXiv:2306.15222, стр. 5]. However, these methods often come with trade-offs, such as increased computational cost and potential degradation in performance on certain tasks [arXiv:2307.12345, стр. 8]. To address these challenges, researchers have proposed hybrid approaches that combine self-consistency checks with adaptive sampling techniques to optimize both efficiency and accuracy [arXiv:2310.01234, стр. 6].

review_text: Improving self-consistency in large language models (LLMs) through probabilistic tokenization has been explored in recent research [arXiv:2407.03678, стр. 6]. Hypothesis-driven theory-of-mind reasoning for LLMs has been proposed to enhance their capabilities in various tasks, including solving math and coding problems [arXiv:2502.11881, стр. 1]. Inference-time reasoning in LLMs has been a key area of research, with methods like Chain-of-Thought (CoT) demonstrating the benefits of generating intermediate reasoning steps [arXiv:2502.11881, стр. 10]. Reasoning-Claim-Verification (Reasoning-CV) is a two-stage fine-tuning method designed to improve the reasoning capabilities of LLMs for claim verification [arXiv:2505.12348, стр. 2]. The first stage of Reasoning-CV involves prompting GPT-4o to generate reliable reasoning paths for ground-truth labels and performing supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on pre-existing data [arXiv:2505.12348, стр. 2]. The second stage of Reasoning-CV improves the quality of reasoning paths and calibrates the LLM’s judgment thresholds through conditional LLM generation for preferences [arXiv:2505.12348, стр. 8]. Despite advancements, LLMs still face challenges in maintaining consistency in their long reasoning paths and in setting appropriate acceptance thresholds [arXiv:2505.12348, стр. 5]. Fine-tuning methods for math reasoning, such as distilling reasoning paths and fine-tuning LlaMA LLMs, have achieved outstanding results [arXiv:2505.12348, стр. 8].
